audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven side tokens contradicted the why beneath them: whys[0] gives Level 1 to Tahm but win[0] read Graves; whys[1] and whys[2] describe Graves' punish window but read Skill and Tahm Kench; whys[4] literally says the two 'cancel into a skill check' but read Graves.
audit.why: The packet chart — Tahm Kench / Graves / Graves / Tahm Kench / Skill / Tahm Kench / Tahm Kench — matches the reasoning and the 39.13% Emerald+ win rate: Graves owns levels 2-3 and nothing else.
audit.corrected: Chart set to the packet in both layers, phase whys rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer phase whys were generic Graves boilerplate and never named the ability that actually defines each stage.
audit.why: The real stage drivers are Tongue Lash (900 range, 5-7s, heals him on champion hit), Abyssal Dive (W, 1000-1200 range, 17-21s, knockup, and his only escape), and Thick Skin (E, 3s, converts stored damage into a shield). Graves' level 6 is a kill threat that one full Thick Skin shield absorbs.
audit.corrected: All seven phase whys rewritten around those abilities with real ranges and cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Slot assignments are wrong across nine fields. Devour is called his W ('W devour', 'W self-devour', 'W-devours you'); Thick Skin's shield is called a 'W self-shield'; Abyssal Dive is labelled '(E)' and credited with a non-existent 'self-stun setup'; and the stun is attributed to a 'double Tongue Lash'.
audit.why: Riot's kit: W is Abyssal Dive, 'Dive down and then re-appear at target location, damaging and knocking up all enemies in an area.' E is Thick Skin, 'Passive: stores a percent of the damage he takes and heals based on it while out of combat. Active: Convert all stored damage into a temporary shield.' R is Devour. The stun is An Acquired Taste: damage builds stacks, and 'If the champion already has 3 stacks... they are stunned' when Q hits.
audit.corrected: Every reference re-pointed to the correct slot, matching the fix already made on the Tahm Kench side of this matchup, and the stun condition restated as three stacks rather than two Q hits.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Grey health' is described as regenerating your burst back mid-fight — 'before his grey health refills', 'grey health regenerates your burst'.
audit.why: Thick Skin's passive heal happens WHILE OUT OF COMBAT; in a fight the stored damage is only available as a shield on the active. That changes the play: you are not racing a mid-fight heal, you are racing whether he has banked enough to shield, and disengaging is what actually gives him the value back.
audit.corrected: Rewritten as a stored-damage shield throughout, with the out-of-combat heal implied by 'don't let him reset'.

edits.before: "Level 1 is his: Tongue Lash out-ranges your point-blank shells, so he chips you for free while you have only one magazine and no E to close the gap. The instant you hit 2 and especially 3 that flips, E in for the full point-blank shell spread, drop Smoke Screen on top of him to cut his vision and zone, and burst with Q-detonate plus autos before his grey health refills. The whole early game is respecting that Tongue Lash, because a double-tap stuns you in melee and he W-devours you or eats a gank while you have no E charge left to dash out."
edits.after: "Level 1 is his: Tongue Lash reaches 900 and heals him on hit, so he chips you for free while you have only one magazine and no E to close the gap. The instant you hit 2 and especially 3 that flips, E in for the full point-blank shell spread, drop Smoke Screen on him to cut his sight range and zone, and burst with Q-detonate plus autos before Thick Skin banks it. The whole early game is respecting An Acquired Taste: every hit stacks it, and the Q that lands the third stack stuns you — then Devour (R) or a gank finishes while your E is spent."

edits.before: "Levels 4-5 are where it sours: his grey-health passive starts healing your bursts back faster than your True Grit stacks matter, so trades that should win for you just regenerate on his side. At 6 your Collateral Damage adds a real kill threat, but he gets nothing to fear from a single nuke when grey health and W self-shield absorb it, so only commit the full Q-E-R when his Tongue Lash is down and his grey bar is already spent. Burn your E charges weaving autos to keep your armor/MR up, because a clean stun chain from him ends you."
edits.after: "Levels 4-5 are where it sours: Thick Skin banks a share of everything you deal and hands it straight back as a shield, so trades that should win for you come out level. At 6 your Collateral Damage adds a real kill threat, but a full stored-damage shield absorbs a single nuke, so only commit the whole Q-E-R when his Tongue Lash is down and that shield is already spent. Keep weaving autos to refund Quickdraw's cooldown and hold your armor up, because three An Acquired Taste stacks into a stun ends you."

edits.before: "This is the lane you cannot win late. His W devour deals percent-max-HP and his grey-health passive both scale past your stacked armor and MR, so the longer fights go the worse your math gets against a drain tank. Your one path is the first-item Eclipse/Youmuu's window: force every all-in there, snowball a lead off your level 2-3 and 6 spikes, and close the game before two items turn him into an unkillable sustain wall that out-lasts your entire shell magazine."
edits.after: "This is the lane you cannot win late. Devour is his R and it removes you from the fight outright, while Thick Skin turns everything you deal into his next shield, so the longer fights go the worse your math gets against a drain tank. Your one path is the first-item Eclipse/Youmuu's window: force every all-in there, snowball a lead off your level 2-3 and 6 spikes, and close the game before two items turn him into a sustain wall that out-lasts your entire shell magazine."

notes: This page had Tahm Kench's slots scrambled in nine places — Devour called his W, Thick Skin's shield called a 'W self-shield', Abyssal Dive labelled '(E)' with an invented 'self-stun setup'. The Tahm Kench side of the mirror was corrected the same way, so the two pages now agree. Second substantive fix: Thick Skin's heal is out-of-combat only; in a fight the stored damage is a shield, so the advice 'burst him before his grey health refills' was describing a mechanic that does not run mid-fight. Both packet suspectNames are false positives — Tongue Lash and Collateral Damage are the correct names.
